interpretations.text: Observation — The new native-control diagnostic found no improvement over its recorded baseline: baseline and best schedules both had holding maximum position error 0.010000000000387073 m, holding maximum speed 0.030000000000649462 m/s, terminal position error 0.009764699817034386 m, and normalized signed maximum excess 3.870725961974131e-11. The strict worst failure was holding position at time 0.5400000000000004 s: 0.010000000000387073 m against the 0.01 m limit. Holding speed also had a positive normalized excess of 2.1648682846375777e-11. Thus the sampled model predicates failed, although only by extremely small strict violations. This result covers 31 samples over 0–0.6 s in the declared native model; it is diagnostic rather than task acceptance. The computation used 145 optimization evaluations and rollouts, 13 started iterations, and 87,000 physics steps.

Evidence — Within this specific 18-coefficient, three-knot local search from one recorded start, the hypothesis that local control adjustment would improve every registered sample is weakened: the best metrics were identical to the baseline, the stop reason was stagnation, and the search radii fell below the declared minimum. Lower-bound input saturation occurred, but there was no upper saturation or coefficient-boundary hit. These observations can indicate a limitation of the local parameterization, start, or search process; they do not identify any one cause. In particular, finite-search stagnation and lower-bound saturation do not establish structural infeasibility, because other legal controls and representations were not excluded and no mechanism result was bound to the best-control trajectory.

Unresolved — Two explanations remain distinguishable but untested: (1) another legal control representation or start could remove the sampled violations, predicting a lower signed excess under expanded control-search evidence; failure across broader, independently recorded searches would weaken this explanation. (2) the candidate may lack sufficient task-relevant authority, predicting persistent failures together with trajectory-bound drive or braking limitations; a passing independent replay or evidence of adequate remaining authority would weaken that explanation. Parameterization, search scale, initialization, and model-versus-replay differences are confounders. Independent full 0-to-duration replay, frozen task acceptance, geometry observations, and best-trajectory mechanism evidence are missing, so neither task success nor global or structural infeasibility can be concluded.

scientific_interpretation.prediction_difference: Match candidate, task, actual control, initial state, input channels and time grid before computing model prediction differences.
scientific_interpretation.research_hypothesis: A proposed mechanism needs subsequent observations that can support or weaken it.
